issues.description: The UML in the problem statement defines Animal with two attributes (name: String and age: int) and a constructor Animal(String, int), but the provided solution implements Animal with only a name and a constructor Animal(String). The template's Main (commented example) also instantiates animals using single-argument constructors (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle")). This inconsistency leaves students unsure whether they must implement Animal (and subclasses) with an age field and a two-argument constructor or with only a name and single-argument constructors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor/attributes consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement/UML to remove the age attribute and specify Animal(String) as the constructor (and update UML diagram accordingly), or (B) Update the template and solution to include the age attribute and use Animal(String, int) (adjust subclass constructors and the example instantiations in Main to pass an age). Ensure the example code in Main matches the chosen constructor signature so students have a clear reference.
